title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description: Given an `m x n` integer matrix, whenever an element is `0`, set its **entire row and column** to `0`. Do this in place; the method returns nothing. Only zeros that were in the original matrix trigger this, not zeros you create along the way. Try to use O(1) extra space.
hints: If you zero cells as you find zeros, you cannot tell old zeros from new ones. Record first, modify later.
Sets of zero rows and zero columns work in O(m + n) space. Can the matrix's own first row and first column store those flags?
Use row 0 and column 0 as markers, remembering separately whether row 0 and column 0 originally contained a zero. Zero the inner cells from markers, then handle row 0 and column 0 last.

solution.explanation: Use the matrix's first row and first column as flag storage. First note whether row 0 or column 0 already contains a zero. Then for every other cell that is zero, mark its row's first cell and its column's first cell. Next zero every inner cell whose row or column marker is zero. Finally zero row 0 and column 0 if they originally held a zero. Every cell is visited a constant number of times: O(m*n) time and O(1) extra space.
